items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I was working with a drummer named Johnny Johnston, and the piano player who played with him was an excellent pianist Johnny Van(?).

ctx.x: And a friend of mine...well, one of the guys from home who had played Don Dunbar's orchestra, Simon(?) Jefferson, he invited me to play...to come down and play with him on his gig at a place on St. Antoine, just below Adams in Detroit, called the Turf Bar. And they had one of those bandstands behind the bar, high bandstands, you know. So I used to go down and sit in with him. So eventually, I started making myself a little name around the city. So I started getting calls on different kinds of gigs and things.

I remember one gig I played that was kind of interesting. I played out on Eight-Mile Road at Jack Johnson's, the ex-heavyweight champion's place, and he was like the host. And we had a very fine group there. I was working with a drummer named Johnny Johnston, and the piano player who played with him was an excellent pianist Johnny Van(?). Johnny Van was quite a guy.
